|BearSSL
|by design: `+aes_ct64+` and `+ghash_ctmul64+`, or AES-NI and PCLMUL where the CPU has them; on a 32-bit host a 64-bit multiplication may not be constant time, which BearSSL documents; link:https://www.bearssl.org/constanttime.html[BearSSL, constant-time crypto]; link:https://www.bearssl.org/ctmul.html[BearSSL, constant-time multiplications]

|OpenSSL
|with assembly (native Clang and GCC), AES-NI and carry-less multiplication where the CPU has them; built no-asm (MSVC, wasip2, wasip3), table-based AES and 4-bit GHASH, neither constant time (`+OPENSSL_AES_CONST_TIME+` makes only the AES core constant time; GHASH stays table-based); link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/INSTALL.md[OpenSSL's INSTALL.md, no-asm]; link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/aes/aes_core.c[OpenSSL's crypto/aes/aes_core.c, OPENSSL_AES_CONST_TIME]
|not measured yet

|libsodium
|by its documentation for the paths crypto calls, without a guarantee for the whole library: secrets are compared in constant time (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/internals#branches[libsodium's documentation, internals: branches]), ChaCha20 is not sensitive to timing attacks (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead[libsodium's documentation, AEAD constructions: ChaCha20 and timing attacks]), and Ed25519 and X25519 come from designs with no secret branch and no secret array index (link:https://ed25519.cr.yp.to/[Ed25519's design: no secret branch conditions, no secret array indices]); webcpp's lane checks each path it calls

Measured where a family differs from its backend's design:

* X25519 on libsodium, wasip2: an open finding, measured and not explained: dudect times `+agree+` with an all-zero secret key against random ones at |t| 13 to 32, against the threshold 10 (a fixed key against another fixed key: 22.9), under wasmtime 47 on an Apple M5, from a release build (2026-11-18), where the native builds pass (|t| 2 to 4); no branch on a secret was found in the WebAssembly or in wasmtime's compiled code, and the cause is unknown. The lane prints this value on wasip2 without judging it; the CI's x86-64 run measures it next
